title: Non-Degenerate Conic Brianchon from the Hexagon Ratio Algebra

problemStatement.formal: If a hexagon $A_1B_1C_1A_2B_2C_2$ is circumscribed about a non-degenerate conic $\mathcal{C}$, then its three principal diagonals are concurrent (Brianchon). Ratio-algebraically: the six tangent-contact side-measures of the circumscribed hexagon satisfy the closure reciprocity $P(\mathrm{cfg}) \cdot P'(\mathrm{cfg}) = \frac{bd}{dc}\frac{ce}{ea}\frac{af}{fb} \cdot \frac{dc}{ce}\frac{ea}{af}\frac{fb}{bd} = 1$, now for a genuine non-degenerate conic rather than the degenerate two-geodesic (Pappus) conic, uniformly for length, $\sin$, and $\sinh$ measures.
problemStatement.plain: The source entry proved the algebraic core of Pappus-Brianchon only for the degenerate conic (two geodesics carrying the alternating hexagon vertices), which is the Pappus special case. This problem asks to lift that same telescoping ratio invariant to a genuine non-degenerate conic, so the six tangent-contact measures of a circumscribed hexagon still satisfy P*P' = 1 and the concurrence of the three principal diagonals is exactly Brianchon's theorem -- delivered uniformly for Euclidean, spherical (sin), and hyperbolic (sinh) measures.
whyMatters: Brianchon's theorem (1810) is the projective dual of Pascal's hexagram and a cornerstone incidence result of conic geometry; the source entry deliberately handled only the degenerate (Pappus) case and left the genuine-conic Brianchon statement as explicit future work.

Because the closure reciprocity holds verbatim for sin and sinh measures, promoting it to a non-degenerate conic would yield the spherical and hyperbolic Brianchon theorems simultaneously from one verified ratio-algebraic engine.

proven: The hexagon closure relation ceva_dual_reciprocal (P*P' = 1) for the degenerate conic, formalized in cevas-theorem-non-euclidean-oq-03.

The abstract Ceva-Brianchon duality ceva_iff_dual and the multiplicative chaining laws cevaProduct_comp, dualProduct_comp, ceva_comp_of_ceva, plus spherical/hyperbolic closure instances via the parent's sin/sinh measure builders.
Non-Euclidean Menelaus (cevas-theorem-non-euclidean-oq-02), the transversal companion supplying the concurrence/collinearity criteria.
open: No formalization of the six tangent-contact side-measures for a hexagon circumscribed about a genuine non-degenerate conic.
No proof that the closure reciprocity P*P' = 1 survives the passage from two geodesics (degenerate conic) to a genuine conic.
No Lean statement of Brianchon concurrence of the three principal diagonals for the non-degenerate case in any of the three constant-curvature geometries.
knownResults.goal: Define a NonDegenerateConicHexagon configuration whose six positive measures are the tangent-segment measures of a hexagon circumscribed about a conic, prove the closure relation P*P' = 1 for it by reusing the telescoping argument, and derive the Brianchon concurrence condition; then specialize verbatim to sin (sphere) and sinh (hyperbolic) via the parent's measure builders. Full projective incidence (points and lines) is a stretch goal.
